building.quote: ORDINANCE NO. 3808-C.S. AN ORDINANCE REPEALING AND REPLACING CHAPTER 1, "BUILDING CODE," OF TITLE 9, "BUILDING REGULATIONS" OF THE MODESTO MUNICIPAL CODE TO ADOPT BY REFERENCE THE 2025 CALIFORNIA BUILIDNG CODE ... WHEREAS, the City is not proposing any amendments to the California Building Code ... each and all of the regulations, provisions, penalties, conditions and terms of said 2025 California Building Code on file in the Office of the Chief Building Official of the City of Modesto is hereby referred to, adopted and made a part hereof ... be and hereby is adopted as the Building Code of the City of Modesto. ... building.note: Read in the City Clerk's 2026 ordinance book (a 16 MB scanned PDF with a text layer). Section 9-1.101 as printed says the file copy is 'marked and designated as the 2022 California Building Code' and later 'said 2025 California Building Code': a drafting slip in the ordinance; the title, the article heading and the rest of the section say 2025. The same ordinance adopts the 2025 California Residential Code and Green Building Standards Code. The state code's own effective date (January 1, 2026) was not re-read on a state page for this pack; it is quoted in the Sacramento pack from that city's page.

fixtures.text: Ordinance No. 3809-C.S. replaces the whole of Modesto's plumbing code chapter with one section adopting the 2025 California Plumbing Code, and recites that the city proposes no amendments. Table 422.1 and section 422 therefore apply as the state publishes them, and the state pack's worked examples stand. No city handout on fixture counts was found on the Building Safety pages (the document links on those pages returned 404).

Modesto publishes no exempt-work list of its own that could be read: its building code chapter is the state code adopted without amendments (Ordinance No. 3808-C.S.), and the Building Safety pages give only two FAQ answers, which match the state list.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Modesto job sites. Price your restroom in five questions and see the California rules Modesto applies.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Modesto food processing plants, schools, medical offices and warehouses, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Modesto uses California's rules, which set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Modesto uses California's building rules without changes, including the state's list of work that needs no permit. That list covers "painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, countertops and similar finish work" and movable "partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches" high. It doesn't name toilet partitions, so ask the Building Safety Division (209-577-5232) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the City of Modesto Building Safety Division
page.stalls_intro: Modesto counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and California's rules require urinals in the men's room. Every toilet needs a stall, and urinals need screens between them. The women's room must have at least as many toilets as the men's room has toilets and urinals together.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for new buildings, additions and changes of use that bring in more people. An office or shop with 50 people or fewer may have a single one-person restroom. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, California's plumbing rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, and a restaurant dining room or a classroom at one per 30 square feet. Your architect or the City of Modesto Building Safety Division sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Contractors with a place of business in Modesto pay the city's contractor business license tax. California requires its contractor license, usually the C-61/D-34 class, for partition installs of $1,000 or more, and at any price when the job needs workers or a permit. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: In Modesto the contractor needs a California contractor license for jobs of $1,000 or more.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** California requires the state-set wage on public jobs over $1,000, including city and school district work. For a carpenter in Stanislaus County that is $67.23 an hour plus $34.95 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.875% in Modesto: 7.25% statewide, 0.125% for the county library, 0.5% for county roads and 1% city.
page.buyers_extra: - **Food and beverage processing plants:** solid plastic (HDPE) or stainless steel for employee restrooms and locker rooms.

- Modesto permits and exempt work: 2025 California Building Code section 105.2, adopted without amendments by [Ordinance No. 3808-C.S.](https://www.modestogov.com/Archive.aspx?ADID=4507) and read on a [secondary copy (UpCodes)](https://up.codes/viewer/california/ca-building-code-2025/chapter/1/scope-and-administration); City of Modesto, [Building Safety Division](https://www.modestogov.com/564/Building-Safety-Division) (permit FAQs and phone number) and [Building Permits](https://www.modestogov.com/1281/Building-Permits). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Modesto sales tax: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration, [city and county rates effective October 1, 2026](https://cdtfa.ca.gov/taxes-and-fees/rates.aspx), [CDTFA-95](https://cdtfa.ca.gov/formspubs/cdtfa95.pdf) and [CDTFA-105, District Taxes, Rates, and Effective Dates](https://cdtfa.ca.gov/formspubs/cdtfa105.pdf). Checked 2026-11-24.
